entries.claim: The common domain of two or more algebraic fractions is the set of real numbers where the fractions are identified together completely (at the same time).
entries.quote: The set of real numbers where the fractions are identified together completely

entries.claim: If $n_1$ and $n_2$ are two algebraic fractions, the domain of $n_1=R-X_1$ (where $X_1$ is the set of zeroes of the denominator of $n_1$) and the domain of $n_2=R-X_2$ (where $X_2$ is the set of zeroes of the denominator of $n_2$), then the common domain of the two fractions is $R-(X_1\cup X_2)$ = R - the set of zeroes of the two denominators of the two fractions.

entries.claim: The common domain of a number of algebraic fractions = R - the set of zeroes of the denominators of these fractions.
